title: Question
description: Something nobody has settled yet, and the answer once there is one.
guidance: Raise one before asking a person, not after: a question written down outlives the conversation, and the answer lands where the next reader finds it. The title is the question itself and ends in a question mark; the body says what prompted it and what each option costs. Link with `references` to whatever it is about — a question read with nothing beside it is answered by guessing. Offer `options` whenever the answer is a choice: the ones taken are written back into `chosen`, and `answer` says in prose what settled it. Answer it in place rather than opening a second record.

status.description: Whether it is still a fork.

options.description: The choices offered, when the answer is a choice rather than free text.

multi_select.description: Whether more than one option may be chosen.

chosen.description: The options that were taken, spelled exactly as `options` spells them. Empty while the question is open, and empty for an answer that was prose rather than a choice. It is a field rather than a sentence inside `answer` because what was chosen is the half a list can show and a reader can count; the prose beside it is the half that says why.

answered_by.description: The decision this question was resolved into.

references.description: What the question is about — the task, the claim or the document it came out of. This is the context whoever answers reads first.
